finding: V22/V25 require a durable provider-intent record before the first remote operation, including the first request in a conversation and compaction (V26). The exact current ConversationSegment shape cannot represent a brand-new pre-provider operation without inventing account_id/notion_thread_id/turn-progress fields that do not exist yet. Overloading ConversationSegment with fake provider identity creates an avoidable risk that rollover/anchor/diagnostic code interprets a tombstone as a real remote segment. A dedicated content-free provider_intents ledger in the same atomic state document removes that ambiguity and naturally separates V25 retention/capacity from ordinary conversation TTL/LRU.

preferred_shape.conversations: real provider segment + exact replay only after provider result is known
preferred_shape.atomic_finalize: one strict state write creates/updates real conversation+replay and removes the matching provider_intent

required_invariant: A new conversation can publish a provider intent before account lease/provider entry without fabricating account_id or notion_thread_id.
Any unresolved intent for a conversation blocks every provider-entering request on that conversation until explicitly reconciled or atomically finalized.
General conversation TTL/LRU never deletes provider_intents; V25's independent unresolved-intent bound applies to this ledger.
Successful final publication atomically writes the real segment/progress/exact replay and clears the matching intent in the same NCM28 state write.
If final publication fails, the prior durable intent remains and no partial/fake conversation segment is committed.
Compaction uses the same ledger and rules as ordinary Responses (V26).
interaction_with_v27: The dedicated provider_intents top-level field must be introduced only in the new durable-state schema epoch after the V27 compatibility floor. Keeping it under outer version=2 is downgrade-unsafe because the exact current v2 loader/save pair drops unknown top-level fields.
